parakeet: I spent years inside church culture. I've seen the green rooms, the staff meetings, the giving campaigns, the sermon planning, the volunteer pressure, the conference language, the leadership books, and the way ordinary organizational mechanics get baptized as miracles. And once you've seen enough of it, you realize megachurches are not proof that God is moving. They're proof that systems work, even when you're being dishonest about the systems at work. Mega churches don't grow because a God is uniquely moving in one building. They grow because certain systems scale. Branding, emotional engineering, volunteer labor, donor psychology, charismatic authorities, stagecraft, leadership pipelines, and organizational control. The tragedy is that these systems are often baptized as anointing, favor, or revival, when in reality they're human mechanisms being treated as divine proof. Before we get into this, this is not a blanket statement about every megachurch, every pastor or every person who attends one. There are sincere people in these spaces. There are pastors who mean well. There are members who genuinely find community there. But sincerity doesn't erase systems. What I'm naming here are observable patterns in high growth church culture. Patterns I've seen, patterns I've studied, and patterns I've lived close enough to to recognize. And if you don't believe me, this was me just 12 years ago.
